# EdFringeNow — the data pipeline (scraper/ and data/)

The domain of this pack: getting show data out of edfringe.com and into the
committed files the site serves. Read it before touching `scraper/` or anything
under `data/`. The API's own field reference lives in
[scraper/SCRAPING.md](../../../../scraper/SCRAPING.md) and the file layout in
[scraper/README.md](../../../../scraper/README.md) — this is the working
judgment those two don't carry.

## The live API is unreachable from a session — don't try, and don't fake it

`edfringe-tikketr-web-api.equhost.com` is blocked by the sandbox egress proxy
(403 at the CONNECT). So: no session — this one included —
can verify a scraper change against live data. Anything that must touch the API
runs through a sanctioned workflow: the `Scrape edfringe shows (full)` workflow
(`.github/workflows/scrape.yml`), `Fetch ticket prices (one-off)`
(`prices.yml`), or the `refresh-shows` / `refresh-tickets` scheduled tasks.
Never "verify" a scraper change by reasoning about what the API probably
returns — either have a sanctioned workflow run it, or say plainly that it is
unverified.

The egress block is a **policy boundary, not an obstacle to route around**. Do
not create ad-hoc GitHub Actions workflows — push-triggered "probes" or
anything else — to reach the API (or any blocked host) from an open-network
runner: that is CI as a side channel around the session's network rules.

For one-off API questions (a field's shape, an enum's value set, whether an
operation exists at all), `scraper/SCRAPING.md` is the reference. When it falls
short there is one legitimate source short of asking the owner:
**`www.edfringe.com` itself is reachable**, and its Next.js bundles carry the
client's complete GraphQL operation set — every query, mutation and fragment,
with full field selections. Recipe in SCRAPING.md ("Reaching it from a Claude
Code web session"). That is reading a public asset from an allowed host, and it
is how the "no bulk price endpoint" claim was finally settled. It tells you what
a query would look like, never what it returns — so a change checked only that
way is still unverified against live data and must be reported as such. If that
doesn't answer it either, ask the repo owner rather than building a bypass.

`python3 scraper/normalize.py --selftest` is the one transform check that runs
offline; it exercises raw→master→day-file→`shows.min.json` on a fixture, so a
normalizer change is verifiable here even though a fetch change is not. Because
it is the only offline verification a scraper change can get, it must stay wired
into `scripts/verify.sh` — the `edfringe-normalizer-selftest-in-verify` check
enforces that (a step *label* naming the self-test does not count; only a command
line does).

## `ticketStatus`, never the `soldOut` boolean

"Can I get a ticket" comes from the per-performance `ticketStatus`, not the
`soldOut` flag: a performance can be `soldOut: false` and still have nothing to
sell online (`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE`). The site treats `SOLD_OUT` and
`NO_ALLOCATION_CONTACT_VENUE` as unavailable and everything else as available
(`NO_TICKETS_STATUSES` in `js/app.js`), and unknown means available. Any new
availability logic — client or scraper — keys off `ticketStatus`; `soldOut` is
carried through for display only.

## A price belongs to a performance, not to a show

The same run sells at several prices: previews cheaper than the main run,
weekends dearer than weekdays. The first price pass didn't know that — it
called `performancePrices` for **one** performance per show and filed the answer
under the show. Pre-festival the performance it picked was almost always the
earliest, i.e. a preview, so **1,016 of 3,664 priced shows (28%) published their
cheapest night as their price**: Alfie Brown's £15/£16 run shipped as £8.50.

The fix is not a rule about previews, and adding a "skip previews" or
"price after date X" heuristic re-creates the same class of bug from a different
angle — it still picks one performance and hopes it represents the rest.
**Price every performance.** There is no bulk price *field*, but GraphQL aliases
make one request carry a whole show's run (`fetch_prices.prices_query`), so full
per-night pricing costs roughly the same ~3,700 requests as the old pass. There
is no call budget to economise against here, so don't design as if there were.

Which payload gets which number is the load-bearing distinction:

| payload | question it answers | price |
|---|---|---|
| master, `shows.min.json` (planner) | what does this *show* cost? | run-wide `priceMin`..`priceMax` |
| `data/days/*.json` (Now page) | what does it cost *tonight*? | that performance's own `pm` |

A performance the cache has no entry for gets **no `pm` at all** — "Price TBC" —
rather than the show's minimum. Borrowing a neighbouring night's figure is
exactly the bug above, and a lower bound presented as the price is a lie about
money even when every number in it is real.

## Prices are fetched once, and "unknown" is a third state the encoding must keep

`data/prices.json` is a fetch-once cache (`scraper/fetch_prices.py`), off the
nightly path: a show's price bands are set when it goes on sale, unlike its
ticket status. `refresh-shows` reads the cache and carries the amounts through
untouched — it never re-fetches them. So the festival keeps adding shows the
cache has never seen, and **a show with no price is a normal, permanent state of
the data**, not a gap the pipeline should close.

The cache carries two entry shapes and both must stay readable: current entries
have `sets` + `perfs` (per performance), and entries from the old pass have a
bare whole-show `min`/`max`. The migration completes one show per re-run, so
dropping the legacy shape — or emptying the cache to "start clean" — would blank
every price on the site until a full pass finished. `price_sets` reads both.

Which means the encoding carries three states, not two, and every stage has to
preserve the distinction:

| state | master | wire |
|---|---|---|
| costs nothing | `priceMin: 0` | `pm: 0` |
| priced | `priceMin: 22.5` | `pm: 22.5` |
| unknown | `priceMin: null` | no `pm` key at all |

`priceMin: 0` and `free: true` are **not** the same claim and don't always agree.
The flag comes from the listing; the £0 can also come from the price API, which
returns a single `Price band 1` at £0.00 for a handful of shows the listing
doesn't flag free — pay-what-you-want, or a box office that never set a price
(10 of 3,664 in the first full run). Both readings are honest about what a ticket
costs, so the price path keys off `priceMin`, and `free` stays what the *listing*
said. Don't "fix" one to match the other.

Never encode unknown as `0`, and never let a decoder default it to one: a stage
that collapses three states into two is lying about money, and nothing
downstream can recover the difference. What the site then *does* with an unknown
price is a product decision, not a pipeline one — it lives in `shared/price.js`.

Two traps in the raw price payload, both already handled and both worth not
re-introducing: amounts arrive as **strings**, and nearly every show carries a
£0.00 "Personal Assistant" concession (a carer's companion ticket) that must not
be read as the cheapest price. See the pricing section of
[scraper/SCRAPING.md](../../../../scraper/SCRAPING.md).

## The API stamps performances in UTC — cross the zone once, at the edge

The listing API's `dateTime` is a real UTC instant (`"2026-08-06T11:45:00.000Z"`),
**not** Edinburgh wall-clock with a decorative `Z`. Slicing the digits out of that
string is the trap: it looks like it works — every date and time in it is
plausible — and in August it is silently an hour wrong for the whole catalogue.
That is exactly what shipped, and what #275 cost to undo: 60,115 performances
listed an hour early, with the tell being shows that name their own time (a 10am
"Shakespeare for Breakfast" sitting at 09:00).

The pipeline has **one** time-zone crossing, and it is `normalize.local_date_start`.
`refresh_ticket_status.py` and `fetch_prices.py` share it so a performance is keyed
by the same local date and start everywhere. Everything written after it — the
master, `data/days/*.json`, `availability.min.json`, `shows.min.json` — is already
Edinburgh wall-clock, so **no stage downstream parses, converts, or re-offsets a
time**. Treating a stored value as UTC a second time is the same bug from the other
end.

Two consequences to hold on to when touching this:

- **A "now" compared against these times is read in Edinburgh too** — `js/clock.js`
  (`festivalNow` / `festivalDate`), never the device clock. A UK visitor cannot see
  the difference, which is why a device clock survives review; a visitor planning
  from another zone reintroduces the whole drift.
- **A conversion change is a full-snapshot change.** The committed data is generator
  output, so the fix is not complete until the master is rebuilt through the new
  conversion and every derived artifact regenerated from it. Shifting the boundary
  moves performances between day files (two late 31 Aug performances now fall into
  1 Sep, outside the August day files, and live only in the master and the planner's
  catalogue) — expect that and check it, rather than reading it as data loss.

## The committed data is generated output — regenerate it, never hand-edit it

`data/raw_pages/` is a git-ignored regenerable cache. `data/normalized/`,
`data/venues.json` and `data/days/` **are** committed, because the browser
fetches them — but they are still generator output. Fix the data by fixing
`scraper/normalize.py` and re-running it (`--merge` for a top-up, no flag for a
full rebuild from the raw cache); a hand-edit is silently overwritten by the next
`refresh-shows` run and leaves the bug in the generator.

`data/prices.json` is the one exception, and it is an exception to the *direction*
rather than the rule: it is committed, but it is normalize.py's **input**, written
by `scraper/fetch_prices.py`. Nothing regenerates it on a schedule, so nothing
overwrites a hand-edit either — which is precisely why editing it by hand is still
wrong: the edit survives, silently disagreeing with the box office forever. Re-run
the fetch. The `edfringe-data-dir-is-generator-output` check allows it **by name**,
so a second file can't ride in on its shape.

## Changing the wire format is a four-file change

The day files and `shows.min.json` reference `data/venues.json`'s global lists
**by position** (`genre`, `room`, `subs`, `ts`; `g`, `rm`, `sg`, `ar`). That
encoding has one producer and two decoders, and they must move together:

- producer — `scraper/normalize.py` (`build_lookups` / `build_day_files` /
  `minify_master` / `build_availability`)
- decoder 1 — `js/app.js` `adaptShow`, for the day files
- decoder 2 — `plan/lib/hydrate.js` `rehydrateShows`, the exact inverse of
  `minify_master`, round-tripped against the real committed files by
  `plan/lib/__tests__/hydrate.test.mjs`

Add or drop an indexed field and all three change in the same commit. That the
indices still *resolve* is enforced by the `edfringe-lookup-indices` check — it
catches a lookup list regenerated without its day files, but nothing can catch a
decoder left reading the old key, so check both decoders by hand.

Two properties of that encoding are load-bearing for caching, and both fail
silently:

- **The lookup lists are append-only** (`extend_lookup`). The browser holds
  `shows.min.json` for four days and `venues.json` for one, so a stale catalogue
  is routinely decoded against a newer lookup file. An entry that changed index
  would relabel shows' genres and rooms with no error anywhere. Entries are never
  dropped, even once the master stops using them.
- **`shows.min.json` carries nothing that changes through the day.** Ticket
  status lives in `availability.min.json` (its own status list, indexing into
  nothing, so the hourly refresh can rewrite it alone). Putting a status back in
  the catalogue would restart its hourly churn *and* freeze availability for
  anyone holding a cached copy — the bug in #249, re-created from the other end.
  `hydrate.test.mjs` asserts each wire performance carries only `d` and `s`.

The same three-way move applies to plain (non-indexed) wire keys such as the
price fields `pm` / `px`, with one extra hazard: the round-trip test compares the
rehydrated record to the master **as JSON**, so a new master key has to appear in
the *same position* in `normalize_event`'s dict and in `rehydrateShows`'s object
literal. Adding it in one place and appending it in the other fails the
round-trip on key order alone, which reads as a data bug and isn't one.

# edfringe-requirements — the executable-requirements harness here

How this repo runs its spec (`product/requirements.md`) as tests. The framework
conventions are the `executable-requirements` pack; the judgment layer is
`spec-driven-product` + the `writing-tests` skill. This pack carries only what
those don't: the mechanics of a **real-headless-browser** golden harness (the
canon's worked examples render with satori/jsdom or Flutter — this repo is the
first Playwright port) and the local approval/fixture policy. Layout, lanes and
commands live in [product/requirements/README.md](../../../../product/requirements/README.md)
— don't restate them; this file is the judgment and the traps.

## The document reads as pictures

- `product/requirements.md` is scanned by sight: under each visual leaf its
  golden is **visible, uncollapsed**; every textual expansion (acceptance
  notes, proof pointers) is **collapsed** in a `<details>` block. An optimal
  requirements document has almost no words on the page.
- **A visual leaf's statement is a line, not a paragraph.** The golden already
  carries the exact copy, counts, colours and placement — restating them in
  prose only competes with the picture. Say what is being asserted; let the
  image say how it looks. Anything genuinely not visible (a threshold, a rule
  behind the state, a condition that produced it) goes in a collapsed
  **Notes** block, never in the statement.
- **A golden is the smallest surface that proves its leaf** — an element crop,
  a clipped region, or a stitched composite (e.g. one grid lane narrowed to a
  few days, recomposed with its label and verdict columns, no header) — never
  the whole page or even the whole control. The capture recipe lives on the
  case (`capture: "<selector>"` or `capture(page, tools)`; see
  `shared/capture-tools.js`); whole-page capture is a deliberate exception,
  not a default. Scoping is judgment: crop to what the leaf asserts, keep just
  enough surroundings to orient.
- **A change over time is an animation, not a coded assertion.** When a
  requirement is about what an action *changes* — a dismissal that sticks, a
  pick that swaps one card for another — capture the same region before and
  after (and after a reload, where persistence is the point) and play the
  frames as one animated golden (`tools.animate`). A flow is shown as a flow.
  Reserve `stitchV`/`stitchH` for things that are genuinely side by side rather
  than sequential.
- **An animated golden is an APNG, never a GIF** — the choice
  ShoutsAndWhispers made for its sagas, for two reasons that both matter here:
  APNG is lossless, so the golden stays a faithful pixel record of the UI
  instead of a 256-colour approximation of it, and every byte is ours, so the
  comparison stays exact byte-identity. It animates in GitHub markdown exactly
  like a GIF. The encoder is `shared/png.js`'s `encodeAnimated`; the comparator
  detects an animated golden and compares bytes only, since a pixel differ
  reads one still frame and would describe the wrong thing.

## A requirement is a feature, not a module

The spec is organised by what the product *does*, never by how the code is
arranged. "Shared code" is not a requirement category: a rule both front-ends
follow is one feature, and its picture shows **both** the Now page and the
planner — a rule only half the site follows is not the feature. Those
cross-page features sit in their own part **after** the two page-by-page
segments, so each page reads as a whole first.

Cross-page proof is ordinary: a case may navigate between the pages (or open a
second page, when something fixed at context creation — a device timezone —
has to differ) and stitch or animate the surfaces into one golden.

## Prefer several pictures over one coded leaf

Before routing a leaf to `behavior` or `logic`, ask whether it **decomposes
into observable states**. A statement joined by "and" usually does, and each
part is then its own numbered sub-leaf with its own picture — the parent
becomes a heading. The time wheel went this way: "5-minute steps, opens at
now + 2 h, ends at 29:55" was one coded leaf and is now `3.7.1`–`3.7.3`, three
crops anyone can check by eye. Sub-leaves are cheap; a coded assertion the
owner has to read code to trust is not.

Reserve the coded kinds for what genuinely has no picture:

- **`behavior`** — a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes
  downloaded, storage written), or a fact the OS paints rather than the page
  (a native `title` tooltip, a cursor — neither can appear in a screenshot).
- **`logic`** — a pure rule with no rendered surface at all. When the rule is
  about *how values are written*, prefer a **table** over prose: a case may
  declare `table: { columns, rows }`, the gallery renders it into the spec, and
  its `verify()` proves every row against the shipped code — so the table a
  reader sees is generated evidence, not a hand-typed claim.

When a leaf lands in a coded kind *because* the product makes it invisible,
say so in its Notes and name what product change would make it visual — that
is a real finding about the UI, not just a testing limitation.

## The browser is part of the expected

- A golden is only comparable under the **exact Chromium that rendered it**.
  The harness pins the Playwright version and refuses any other
  (`shared/harness/browser.js`); CI installs that pin per run, the Claude
  sandbox ships it globally. **Bumping the pin re-renders every golden** — it
  is a re-baselining, done deliberately and approved like one, never a drive-by
  upgrade.
- When the comparison ever flaps, the fix is **more determinism, not a
  tolerance**: the comparator stays at zero diff. The determinism levers are
  all in one place (the harness): fixed clock via `page.clock`, fixed
  geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network, frozen
  animations, `--font-render-hinting=none --force-color-profile=srgb`.

## Traps this harness already paid for (don't re-derive)

- **Geolocation exists only on secure origins.** The fake origin is `https://`
  — route interception fulfils before any TLS, so no certificate is involved.
  On plain http the app silently keeps its built-in simulated clock and the
  whole render lands on the wrong day.
- **The app adopts the device clock only on an in-UK geolocation fix** — the
  harness's fixed location is central Edinburgh precisely so the pinned clock
  is what renders; deny geolocation (or move abroad) and you are rendering the
  app's own pre-set simulated moment instead, a different day file entirely.
- **A CSS freeze does not stop Web-Animations-API animations.** The planner's
  FLIP board diff runs through `element.animate` — the harness stubs it to
  land on end states; without the stub, captures race the animation.
- **Fonts arrive via the Google Fonts CSS URL**, so the vendored `fonts.css`'s
  `url(/__vendor/…)` references resolve against `fonts.googleapis.com` — the
  vendor route must match on path, host-agnostic, or every glyph silently
  falls back and all text shifts by a pixel.
- **Vendoring the web fonts is only half the font problem.** Every character
  they don't carry — an emoji, `▾`, `≤`, a Cyrillic show title — is drawn from
  the fonts *installed on the machine*, so the goldens quietly become a record
  of the renderer's font set. It cost a red CI lane: the walk-time line
  (`🚶 5 min · £16`) measured wider on the GitHub runner, wrapped, and every
  show card came out 21px taller. The harness now launches Chromium under a
  generated `FONTCONFIG_FILE` whose only font directory is
  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` — the host's fonts cannot reach the page. A new
  emoji or script in the product or the fixtures needs that subset rebuilt
  (see the folder's README), or it renders as tofu.
- **A floating popup dies under a full-page screenshot** (the capture scrolls,
  and scroll dismisses tips/legends/optimizer pops). A popup-state case sets
  `viewportOnly: true` and captures the viewport crop.
- **"Ready" is not `networkidle`.** The pages settle their async work into
  observable state — the footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's
  show count. Wait on those (`case-helpers.js`), plus `document.fonts.ready`.
- **Hover-driven UI must be opened inside `capture()`, not `drive()`.** The
  runner settles the scroll between the two, and scrolling moves an element out
  from under the pointer — which fires `mouseleave` and closes anything the
  hover opened. That is correct product behaviour; the capture just has to
  happen on the right side of it.

## The fixture freeze

- `shared/fixtures/data/` is a snapshot of the **real committed data**, cast by
  the committed builder for state variety (sold-out / free / price-unknown /
  tight / every planner verdict). It is **frozen**: the nightly data refresh
  never touches it, and no case may reach for `data/` live files.
- Every deviation from the source bytes is documented as an `ADJUST` in the
  builder — a fixture edit without one is hand-invented data.
- Re-running the builder re-casts every golden. That is a re-baselining: run it
  only with the owner's approval, and land builder + fixtures + goldens +
  gallery in one reviewed change.

## Golden approval, concretely

- A red screen case is **never** fixed by `refresh:ui`. Surface the committed
  golden, `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png` and `.diff.png`, and ask the
  owner (AskUserQuestion popup, per-item, per the owner's preferences) before
  re-baselining anything.
- A brand-new leaf's golden is a **proposal** until the owner has seen the
  rendering: it lands in the PR diff, and merge approval is the pixel
  approval. Say so in the PR body — the goldens are the review surface.
- An intended UI change lands as: spec edit (doc-first, red) → implementation →
  `npm run refresh:ui` → the refreshed PNGs ride the same diff.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **When there's nothing left to do, say so boldly at the end of the conversation.** Don't bury a "this is complete / I'm blocked / nothing further to do" behind hedging — make the terminal state unmistakable. **Set it apart visually so it catches the eye:** put the terminal state — or, when work remains, the list of open/outstanding items — in its own callout (a Markdown blockquote box, e.g. `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`), not trailing prose the owner has to scan for. One or the other always gets the box: the done-signal when nothing remains, the open-items list when something does.
- **"LGTM"** is the owner's phrase for the merge-to-main command: it asks for the change in front of the owner to be merged into `main`. It's an owner-triggered command; the default mechanics live in the `merge-to-main` skill ([merge-to-main/SKILL.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/git-github/skills/merge-to-main/SKILL.md)) (squash, gate on CI only when the repo has it), and a project that diverges overrides them via a bespoke merge-policy file it names in its own `CLAUDE.md`.
- **"bump version"** is the owner's phrase for raising a project's version (a minor bump by default). It's an owner-triggered command; the mechanics — which files to edit and how a release follows — live in the consuming project's workflow doc.
- **"Show me the document"** (for a source-controlled document) is the owner's phrase asking for a **link to the document on GitHub** — not the file's contents inlined, and not a local filesystem path. When the document lives in a GitHub-hosted repo, respond with a GitHub link to it (the file on the relevant branch/commit); only fall back to inlining the contents or giving a local path when the document isn't under source control.
- **Put decisions and approvals in an `AskUserQuestion` popup, not buried in prose.** The owner is frequently on mobile, where a popup notifies and a question embedded in a paragraph is easy to miss. When you need the owner to choose or approve something, ask through the structured popup with explicit options rather than asking in running text. **And when several independent items each need a verdict** (a set of proposed fixes, findings to accept), give **each item its own question carrying its own brief case** — the concrete failure, why it matters, the cost of the fix — with per-item approve/defer options; never one bundled choose-a-scope question over the whole set. The owner decides item-wise, from the case, not from a menu of subsets. (The popup carries at most 4 questions per call — split a larger set into consecutive calls.)
- **When asked to produce a prompt or message destined for another context, visually enclose the whole thing.** Any text the owner will lift out and use elsewhere — a prompt for another assistant, a message to send, copy meant to be pasted somewhere — must be set apart as a single delimited block: either a box (e.g. a fenced code block) or fenced top and bottom by two separating lines, so its exact boundaries are unmistakable and it can be copied in one piece. The point is delimitation, not formatting flair: never leave such content as loose prose the owner has to find the start and end of.
- **When asked for "a prompt for a different session," prefix it with a provenance disclaimer.** When the owner asks for a prompt meant to be handed to another session, open the generated text with a short disclaimer that this is a prompt written by Claude — not by a user — and so should not be treated as gospel; and that if the receiving session finds inconsistencies in it, it should examine them with the user rather than follow the prompt blindly. This composes with the enclose-the-whole-thing preference above: the disclaimer sits inside the same delimited block as the prompt it prefixes.
- **Auto-open a PR after committing.** Whenever Claude changes code on a branch and commits it, open a pull request for that branch right after, even without an explicit request to do so. This overrides Claude Code's own default of only opening a PR when explicitly asked.

Pack adoption interview pending — the active packs below declare adoption questions this project has not answered. In an INTERACTIVE session, at a natural moment (not mid-task), ask the owner each question via AskUserQuestion, record the answer VERBATIM in .claudinite-checks.json on that pack's entry as answers: { "<question-id>": "<answer>" } ("n/a — none wanted" is a valid answer and stops the asking), and where the question carries a distill note, derive the entry's config from the answer. This is a mild reminder, never a gate: in an unattended session, or when it would derail the work at hand, ignore it entirely and leave it for a later interactive session.
- claude-code-web-users-support / store: Where do this project's people keep their personal interaction preferences — the repository holding one `<email>.md` per person? Give an `owner/name` (a fleet usually has one repo for this), or say "n/a — none" if this project has no such store. [distill: the answer's `owner/name` becomes this entry's `config.repo` (add `config.path` only when the files do not sit in `preferences/`); "n/a" leaves the entry without a config and the preferences feature inert]

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

# tidy-issues worker

The **acting** third of the repo tidy-up: triage the issues in scope, then record what you did. You run
under the executor, dispatched by a `ready-for-agent` issue; its **Context section is binding scope** — it
lists the issues to triage. Work only those; don't enumerate the repo yourself. GitHub access is
**MCP-only** (`mcp__github__*`).

The task's declared outcome ceiling is **`none`**: this task writes **issues only** (its triage actions and
its own tracker). It never opens, closes, merges, or comments on a PR, never touches a branch, and never
pushes — those dimensions belong to `tidy-prs` and `tidy-branches`, which are assess-only.

## 1. Triage each issue

For each issue in the Context list, run the [single-issue-triage](../../skills/single-issue-triage/SKILL.md)
skill. The skill owns the action ladder and the safeguards: "implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual
ask is true of `main`'s content **now** — verified there and cited, never inferred — and when the check is
inconclusive it **comments, doesn't close**. Collect what each triage did.

## 2. Reconcile this task's tracker

One standing tracker issue per repo, titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Tidy Issues` — found by that
**exact title, never a fuzzy match**; create it **already closed** if absent (never a fresh issue per run,
never a bare number that can dangle). Each dimension keeps its **own** tracker, so three tasks never race
to rewrite one body.

Touch it two ways each run:

- **Rewrite the issue body** to today's **dated** snapshot: the actions taken this run and anything left
  for a human. The body is the live picture — it replaces yesterday's, it doesn't accumulate.
- **Add a dated comment** with today's status, so the body's snapshots leave a per-run trail.

Keep both short. **Never open, close, or reopen the tracker** — its state carries no meaning (the body is
the live picture; the state is just however it was created).

## 3. Retire the legacy tracker (transitional, one line of work)

Repos tidied before the split carry a single combined tracker titled exactly `Claudinite tracker: Repo
Tidy`. If it exists and its body doesn't already say so, rewrite the body to one line pointing at the three
per-dimension trackers (`Tidy Issues`, `Tidy PRs`, `Tidy Branches`) and stop there — nothing else to do on
it, and never open, close, or reopen it. Already pointing at them ⇒ skip. Absent ⇒ skip; never create it.

`model: sonnet` — the implemented-in-`main` call is judgment; the reconcile is mechanical aggregation.

Use when extracting lessons from repo artifacts — the growth-extract task's activity half, or an owner asking what a recent stretch of work taught.
- extract-from-conversations: Mine an agent-user conversation — a captured conversation log or the live session — for friction-driven lessons (misunderstandings, backtracks, measured wall-time waits) and land them in the repo's own local packs. Use when extracting lessons from a session transcript or the conversation-logs branch, or when an owner asks for a retrospective.
- file-placement: Where a file should live — the reference-distance metric, the high-reach code smell, and the mandated-location, test-location and plugin-contract exemptions. Use before placing, moving, or renaming a file, or when reviewing where one lives.
- generate-project-instructions: Decompose a project into its pack facets (working-style class, technology, aspect, domain) and extract its working instructions into reusable canon packs plus the project's own local packs (.claudinite/local_packs/). Use when a project has no established working style yet, or it exhibits a facet no pack covers — during bootstrap of a fresh/empty repo, or on an uplevel request.

32	Keep both short. **Never open, close, or reopen the tracker** — its state carries no meaning (the body is
33	the live picture; the state is just however it was created).

35	## 3. Retire the legacy tracker (transitional, one line of work)
36

Base directory for this skill: /home/user/EdFringeNow/.claude/skills/single-issue-triage

# Single-issue triage

Triage **one** open issue and take the **first** applicable action. This **acts** — but every action
defaults to the reversible option when the check is inconclusive.

- **Already implemented in `main`** → **close** (`completed`) + a one-line comment citing where it
  landed.
- **Conflicts with a current guideline** → label `needs-decision` + a comment naming the conflict.
- **Blocked by another issue** → label `blocked` + a comment `blocked by #N`.
- **Small and quick to do** → label `quick-win` + a comment scoping it.
- **Else** → leave it.

**"Implemented in `main`" means the issue's actual ask is true of `main`'s content _now_** — confirm
it there and cite it. **Never** infer it from a linked PR merging or the issue merely looking done. If
you can't point to it, **comment, don't close.** Create a label if it's missing. Return `{ action,
note }` (action one of closed/needs-decision/blocked/quick-win/left).

{"number":314,"title":"Replace per-file cache TTLs with a published manifest","body":"Follow-up to #309, raised by the owner while reviewing the fix.

## The idea

Publish a manifest listing every downloadable data file and a hash of its contents. Fetch it on each load, and evict exactly the cached entries whose hash has moved.

## Why it's better than what we have

The current TTLs (`shared/data-cache.js`) are guesses about how fast each file changes — four days for the catalogue, one for availability, seven for descriptions. They price the same bet on every file and get it wrong in both directions at once: too long and visitors read stale data, too short and they re-download something that never changed.

A manifest gives **longer caching and fresher data at the same time**, which no TTL can. It also makes #309 structurally impossible: every file is checked against one manifest from one publish, so a visitor can't hold Thursday's catalogue beside Saturday's sidecar.

## Design notes

- **The manifest is the one file that must never carry a TTL.** Nothing can attest to its own freshness — a stale copy carries a valid hash of itself. Caching the manifest doesn't save a round-trip, it moves the staleness up one level and hides it better.
- **Marginal cost is near zero.** The planner already fetches `package.json` uncached on every load for the version pill (visible in the reporter's network trace). The manifest is the same shape of request and could absorb that one.
- **Record the hash, don't re-hash.** Store the manifest hash in the stamps map beside the entry; the freshness check is then a string compare. Re-hashing means pushing megabytes through a digest on the critical path to answer a question the bookkeeping already knows.
- **Written atomically with the assets** — same `write_derived_outputs()` call in `scraper/normalize.py`, so it can't describe a publish that didn't happen.
- **A deploy race is expected**: manifest fetched, deploy lands, asset fetched, hash disagrees. Refetch once and continue; only a mismatch surviving fresh copies of both is a real fault.
- Size is not a substitute for a hash: applying #274's correction to the Aug 7 catalogue changes 0 bytes of 3,140,534 while changing the meaning of every record.

## Relationship to the #309 fix

The join fingerprint shipped in #310 answers *"do these two published files agree with each other?"* — a generator-side question. The manifest answers *"is my cached copy the published one?"* — a client-side one, and the one that actually caused #309.

They overlap but neither subsumes the other. If this lands, the fingerprint and the 90% coverage floor become narrower backstops (a generator publishing a genuinely mismatched pair) rather than the primary defence, and the mismatch-triggered refetch path in `loadCatalogue()` could likely be retired in favour of manifest-driven eviction. Worth revisiting them together rather than leaving three overlapping mechanisms in place.

Guidance captured in `.claudinite/local/packs/static-website/RULES.md` (#310).

{"number":294,"title":"Prices exclude the booking fee edfringe advertises — and the recorded `fee` is wrong","body":"Surfaced while validating #285. Two related things: one is a decision for the owner, the other is a data bug.

## 1. We quote the face price; edfringe quotes face + fee (decision)

The original report in #285 was "tickets are £15 or £16, you show £8.50". The per-performance fix moved that night to **£14.50** — correct as a face price, but still not what the reporter saw.

Their two numbers reconcile exactly once the booking fee is added:

| | face | + fee | what they saw |
|---|---|---|---|
| standard | £14.50 | £16.00 | "16" |
| concession | £13.50 | £15.00 | "15" |

So the site is honest about the band value and silent about the fee, while edfringe advertises the fee-inclusive total. Someone comparing the two sees us understate by £1.50 on almost every show — 6,046 of 6,048 price points in the cache carry a fee.

This is deliberate as designed (`SCRAPING.md`: `feeInTicketPrice: false`, the band value *is* the advertised face price and the fee is charged at checkout), and changing it is not free:

- `PRICE_CAPS` semantics shift — "Up to £15" would start meaning a different set of shows.
- `pm`/`px` currently mean face value to both decoders.
- The fee may not apply uniformly (per ticket vs per transaction — see below), so "total" may not be a single number we can quote.

**Not changing anything without a decision.** The options are roughly: keep face only (status quo), show face with a "+ fee" note, or switch to totals and re-point the filter.

## 2. The recorded `fee` is not the per-ticket fee (bug)

Blocks any of the above, because the number we'd add is wrong.

`booking_fee()` takes `max(transactionFeesPrice)` across a performance's bands. For Alfie Brown that records **£3.00** on all three price points — but only **£1.50** reproduces the £15/£16 the reporter actually saw:

```
face £8.50  + £3.00 = £11.50
face £14.50 + £3.00 = £17.50   (observed: £16.00)
face £13.50 + £3.00 = £16.50   (observed: £15.00)
```

Cache-wide the field is bimodal — £1.50 on 5,480 price points, £3.00 on 566 — which looks less like two fee tiers and more like `max()` sometimes picking up a per-transaction or per-order charge rather than the per-ticket one.

Harmless today: nothing renders `fee`. It has to be right before anything does.

### Next step

Capture a raw `performancePrices` response for a £3.00 show (`--print-raw`, which the workflow doesn't currently expose) and look at `fees[]`, `transactionFeesPrice`, `outsideFeesPrice` and `feeInTicketPrice` together, rather than reducing them to one `max()`.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/294","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-09T00:42:46Z","updated_at":"2026-08-09T04:57:05Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":295,"title":"The site lists shows edfringe has withdrawn — nothing removes them from the master","body":"Surfaced while validating #285, from an unexpected angle: 11 shows came out of the full price pass still carrying their old whole-show price. Checking why turned up something bigger than the prices.

## Finding

**9 of the 11 no longer exist on edfringe.** Their pages 404 and the API rejects their slug outright:

```
RuntimeError: no event returned for slug 'almost-50-and-a-woman'
```

| slug | edfringe |
|---|---|
| `almost-50-and-a-woman` | 404 |
| `the-great-chevalier` | 404 |
| `keaomelemele` | 404 |
| `in-conversation-with-andy-burnham` | 404 |
| `rogier-bak-has-your-back` | 404 |
| `scotland-meets-the-united-states-of-america` | 404 |
| `scottish-comedy-legends-greg-hemphill` | 404 |
| `sharon-wanjohi-work-in-progress` | 404 |
| `two-great-scottish-pianoforte-passacaglias` | 404 |
| `jonny-one-name-like-cher-wip` | 200 |
| `kids-breakfast-klub` | 200 |

They stayed unpriced simply because `--all` walks the live listing and never encounters them — the price pass is working correctly. But they are **still in `data/normalized/shows.json`, still in the day files, and still being served**, with performances dated in the future. `almost-50-and-a-woman` has 9 dates remaining that nobody can buy.

## Cause

`normalize.py --merge` upserts by id and never deletes, and `refresh-shows` runs in merge mode. Nothing in the pipeline ever removes a show that has left the listing, so a withdrawal is invisible: the last successful scrape's record simply persists forever.

This is the mirror image of the price-cache design in #285. There, "a show with no price is normal and permanent" is correct, because the *listing* is authoritative for existence. Here the listing has spoken — the show is gone — and we're ignoring it.

## Why it matters more than 9 rows

Sending someone to a 404 for a show tonight is a worse failure than a wrong price. And the count only grows: this is 9 after one festival week, with nothing to clear them.

## Options

- Full (non-merge) rebuilds already drop them, since the master is replaced — so one scheduled full rebuild would clear the backlog, if `--merge` is only a top-up convenience.
- Otherwise reconcile in `--merge`: mark ids absent from a *complete* listing pass as withdrawn and exclude them from the day files. Must key off a pass known to be complete, or a partial scrape would delete the festival.

Worth deciding which, rather than leaving it to the next full rebuild by accident.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/295","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"comments":2,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-09T00:43:07Z","updated_at":"2026-08-09T04:57:01Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":206,"title":"Adopt the static-website pack — replace the hand-rolled deploy, version bump and whole-root upload","body":"This repo hand-rolls what is now a Claudinite standard: `pages.yml` bumps the version with its own `scripts/bump-version.mjs`, stamps the build info, injects the analytics token, `rm -rf`s the agent-tooling dirs and uploads the **whole repo root** as the Pages artifact.

Adopt `static-website` (canon, merged in missingbulb/Claudinite#611) and delete the bespoke halves it replaces:

{"number":237,"title":"Upstream: baselining's deliver() leaves the scheduler checkout on its maintenance branch","body":"Root cause behind #231 and #141, found while correcting #235 (see #236).

The scheduler runs every due task in **one** checkout. `basics/baselining`'s `deliver()` does:

```js
git(['-C', root, 'checkout', '-B', branch]);   // .claudinite/shared/packs/basics/tasks/baselining/worker.mjs:447
```

and never switches back. Every task ordered after a *delivering* baselining in the same run therefore starts on a local branch with no upstream and with baselining's converge commit at HEAD. For this repo's data workers that surfaced as `preprocessing exited 128` on the bare `git push`:

- #231 — run `31016971857`, a manual `FORCE_TASKS=baselining` dispatch: `baselining: ok (agent requested)` then `refresh-tickets: preprocessing exited 128`.
- #141 — `refresh-shows`, on the daily slot baselining shares.

The blast radius is wider than a failed push: any later task that commits is committing onto baselining's branch, and any that pushes by explicit refspec would publish baselining's unreviewed converge past its own maintenance PR.

Two candidate fixes upstream, both local to `deliver()`:
- restore the previous branch after the push (record `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` first, `git checkout -` at the end, including on the failure path); or
- build and push the maintenance commit with plumbing and never touch the working tree — `pushGenerated()` in `deliver-generated.mjs` already does exactly this.

The second matches the engine's own precedent and has no restore-on-failure path to get wrong.

`.claudinite/shared/` is vendored here, so this can't be fixed in this repo — a local edit is clobbered by the next vendor refresh. #236 works around it by returning the checkout to `main` at the top of each edfringe worker.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/237","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-06T16:29:04Z","updated_at":"2026-08-06T16:29:04Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":205,"title":"Maintenance PRs can never auto-merge: pull_request-triggered CI run sits "action_required" forever","body":"Found while running the `basics/baselining` agent stage (dispatch #200), delivering PR #182.

**Symptom:** `maintenance.delivery` is `auto-merge`, but `enable_pr_auto_merge` on PR #182 fails every time with "The pull request is in unstable status (required checks are failing)."

**Root cause (verified via the Actions API):** every `pull_request`-event run of the `CI` workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`, job `verify`) on a Claudinite maintenance branch completes with conclusion `action_required` instead of running — it never posts a status. This has now happened on at least two consecutive cycles:

- run `30606438314` (`pull_request`, commit `0527896`, 2026-07-31) — `action_required`
- run `30685066914` (`pull_request`, commit `cf3f20b`, 2026-08-01) — `action_required`

In both cases the *same* commit's `workflow_dispatch`-triggered run (`30606438304`, `30685065435`) completed with `success` — so the code and the workflow are fine; only the `pull_request` trigger is gated. Both gated runs share `triggering_actor: github-actions[bot]` (the account that opens/updates the maintenance PR), which is the classic shape of a repo's Actions setting **"Require approval for all outside collaborators"** (or similar fork/first-time-contributor approval gate under Settings → Actions → General) mis-treating that bot identity as needing manual approval, even though it's pushing to a branch within this same repo.

**Effect:** since nobody is watching to click "Approve and run" on that specific workflow run, the required check for the branch protection rule never reports, `mergeable_state` stays `unstable`, and `auto-merge` can never arm — every future maintenance PR will sit open indefinitely regardless of content, defeating `maintenance.delivery: auto-merge`.

**Ask:** could you (as repo owner) check Settings → Actions → General → "Fork pull request workflows from outside collaborators" (or the equivalent approval-gate setting) and confirm whether `github-actions[bot]`/this automation should be exempted, or approve the pending run(s) on PR #182 by hand? This is outside what a baselining agent run can fix — no available tool can approve a pending workflow run or change repo Actions settings — so it needs a decision from you.

Refs #200.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/205","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["needs-decision"],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-01T05:12:51Z","updated_at":"2026-08-02T08:01:11Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":208,"title":"One-time GitHub settings for the static-site release pipeline","body":"The release pipeline is vendored and green in CI, but the following are repository *settings* —
nothing in the repo can set them, so they are turned on by hand (Settings → …). Until they are,
the first release-on-push run fails and opens a `workflow-failure` issue.

- [ ] **Pages → Build and deployment → Source = "GitHub Actions"** (not "Deploy from a branch").
      Without it `actions/deploy-pages` fails and nothing is served. The deleted `pages.yml`
      passed `enablement: true`; the vendored deploy does not, so this must be on.
- [ ] **Actions → General → Workflow permissions = "Read and write permissions"**, so the pipeline
      can push the version bump and create the release. (Not needed if the repo is already on
      read/write.)
- [ ] **Environments → `github-pages` → deployment branches** must allow `main` — the default
      "protected branches only" rule already does; check it if the repo renamed its default branch.
- [ ] Optional: **Pages → Custom domain**, if this site has one. Note that a custom domain moves
      the site from `//` to the domain root — see the relative-URL rule in the pack's
      [RULES.md](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/packs/static-website/RULES.md).

Close this issue once the first release-on-push run has deployed successfully.

Pipeline adopted in #207.","state":"open","html_url":"https://github.com/[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]/issues/208","user":{"login":"missingbulb","id":73882448,"profile_url":"https://github.com/missingbulb","avatar_url":"https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/73882448?v=4"},"author_association":"OWNER","labels":["blocked"],"comments":1,"reactions":{"total_count":0,"+1":0,"-1":0,"laugh":0,"confused":0,"heart":0,"hooray":0,"rocket":0,"eyes":0},"created_at":"2026-08-01T06:21:49Z","updated_at":"2026-08-02T08:01:04Z","has_parent":false,"has_children":false}

{"number":164,"title":"Monetization: join Booking.com + Omio and paste the IDs into shared/affiliates.js","body":"The planner's schedule board now carries two partner nags — **"Need a place to sleep?"** in the night zone (below *day ends*) and **"Transportation sorted?"** on the getting-there / getting-out blocks of the first and last day. Both work today as plain deep links and start earning referral commission the moment the IDs are filled in. **All the code is done; the only remaining work is joining the programmes.**

Where the IDs go — the `AFFILIATES` block at the top of [`shared/affiliates.js`](../blob/main/shared/affiliates.js):

```js
export const AFFILIATES = {
  bookingAid: "",              // ← step 1 (Booking.com's own ?aid=)
  bookingClickTemplate: "",    // ← step 1, if you join via a network instead
  omioClickTemplate: "",       // ← step 2
};
```

Partial set-up is fine: each link stays a working untagged deep link until its own ID arrives.

A **click template** is the tracking URL a network's dashboard hands you, pasted verbatim with `{deep}` where the destination goes (it gets URL-encoded for you) — e.g. `https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=9&awinaffid=1234&ued={deep}`, `https://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/destination:{deep}`, `https://tp.media/click?shmarker=1234&promo_id=…&deep_link={deep}`. The shape differs per network, which is why the code takes the real one rather than guessing which programme we end up in.

## 1. Accommodation → Booking.com → `bookingAid` *or* `bookingClickTemplate`

Booking.com is the clear pick for last-minute Fringe beds: the deepest Edinburgh inventory (hotels, apartments, hostels), **4% of completed accommodation stays** as the base rate — rising toward ~40% of Booking's own commission at high monthly volume — and a **30-day cookie**. Four routes in, same destination:

| Route | Approval | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| [Travelpayouts](https://www.travelpayouts.com/) | instant, no traffic minimum | one dashboard/payout shared with Omio in step 2 — **suggested first stop** |
| [Booking.com partner programme](https://www.booking.com/affiliate-program/v2/index.html) (direct) | reviewed | issues the native `aid` |
| [Awin](https://www.awin.com/us/advertisers/partner/booking.com) | days; small refundable deposit | the route [#161](../issues/161) already plans for the Now page; Awin skims a 3.5% tracking fee off commission |
| [CJ](https://www.cj.com/en-gb/publisher/partners/booking.com) | reviewed | alternative network |

- [ ] Join one of the above (Travelpayouts unless there's a reason not to).
- [ ] If the programme issues an **affiliate ID (`aid`)** → paste it into `bookingAid`. If it issues a **tracking link** instead → paste that into `bookingClickTemplate` with `{deep}` in place of the destination URL. Both may apply.
- [ ] Compliance check before applying: Booking.com forbids publishers using "booking"/"agoda"/"priceline" (or misspellings) in the domain name — `edfringenow.com` is clear.
- [ ] Verify: load `/plan`, drop in a favourites file, and check the night-zone nag's URL — it should carry `aid=…&label=edfringenow-plan-night` (the `label` is what separates this nag's earnings from any other placement), and/or be wrapped by the network's domain with the Booking.com search intact inside it.

*Not chosen:* Hostelworld / Agoda / Expedia (all reachable via Travelpayouts) — thinner last-minute Edinburgh inventory, and splitting the click across two accommodation partners halves the attribution for no gain. Revisit only if Booking.com rejects us.

## 2. Transport → Omio → `omioClickTemplate`

The nag sits on the *arrive* and *leave* blocks, where the traveller's question is "how do I get to Edinburgh at all" — not "which train". Omio is the only partner whose one link answers that across every mode, and it prices well:

| Partner | Modes | Reported rate | Network |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Omio** ← chosen | train + coach + flight | ~4% per booking on each mode (reseller networks advertise more) | [Travelpayouts](https://www.travelpayouts.com/blog/earn-with-trainline/) / [Involve](https://app.involve.asia/directory/omio-affiliate-program) / [own programme](https://www.omio.co.uk/affiliate) |
| Trainline | train + coach (UK) | Partnerize rates — third-party listings report ~1–3% of booking value; the "up to 20%" headline is a share of Trainline's own fee revenue, not the ticket | [Partnerize](https://www.thetrainline.com/about-us/partnerships/affiliates) |
| National Express | coach | up to 4% | Awin |
| FlixBus | coach | undisclosed | Awin |
| Skyscanner | flights | revenue share on click-outs; screens for high-volume travel publishers | own / networks |

- [ ] Apply for Omio — via Travelpayouts if step 1 went that way (one account, one payout), otherwise [Omio's own programme page](https://www.omio.co.uk/affiliate).
- [ ] Paste the dashboard's tracking link into `omioClickTemplate`, `{deep}` where the destination goes.
- [ ] Verify: the trip-block nags' URLs should route through the network domain and land on `https://www.omio.com/travel/edinburgh`.

**Fallback if Omio rejects us:** Trainline, whose Partnerize application [#161](../issues/161) already covers — swap `travelLink()`'s destination to the station page that issue verifies (`https://www.thetrainline.com/stations/edinburgh`) and reuse the same `camref` template. Coach-only partners (National Express, FlixBus) aren't worth a placement on their own.

## 3. Reconcile the two ID blocks when #157 lands

[#157](../pull/157) adds a second `AFFILIATES` block in `js/places.js` for the Now page's place pills — including its own Booking.com fields (`awinAffiliateId` / `bookingAwinMid`). One Booking.com account issues **one** set of credentials, so two hand-maintained copies will drift.

- [ ] After #157 merges, delete the Booking.com entries from `js/places.js` and have it import them from `shared/affiliates.js` (the reason that module lives in `shared/`). The other three programmes in #161 — OpenTable, GetYourGuide, Trainline — are Now-page-only and can stay put.
- [ ] Decide the Booking.com route **once** for both pages: `aid` (direct/CJ/Travelpayouts) or the Awin `cread.php` wrapper #161 assumes.

## 4. Confirm the two destination URLs from a network that can reach them

{"number":161,"title":"Monetization: join the 4 affiliate programmes and paste the IDs into js/places.js","body":"The booking buttons on committed places (PR #157, #158) work today as plain deep links and start earning referral commission the moment the affiliate IDs are filled in. All the code is done — `js/places.js` builds every link and tags it automatically once its ID is set. **The only remaining work is joining the programmes**, which each partner runs where *it* chooses (researched 2026-07-29).

Where the IDs go — the `AFFILIATES` block at the top of [`js/places.js`](../blob/main/js/places.js):

```js
export const AFFILIATES = {
  opentableRef: "",      // ← step 4
  trainlineCamref: "",   // ← step 2
  awinAffiliateId: "",   // ← step 1
  bookingAwinMid: "",    // ← step 1
  gygPartnerId: "",      // ← step 3
};
```

Partial set-up is fine: each link stays a working untagged deep link until its own ID arrives. Suggested order = fastest payoff first.

### 1. Booking.com — via Awin (days to approve) → `awinAffiliateId` + `bookingAwinMid`
Booking.com runs its affiliate programme on the Awin network (up to ~4% of the booking).
- [ ] Create an Awin **publisher** account: https://ui.awin.com/publisher-signup/en/awin/step1 — describe EdFringeNow (a free Edinburgh Fringe day-planner that links visitors to hotels near their committed plans). Awin may ask a small refundable deposit to verify you.
- [ ] Once the publisher account is live, find **Booking.com** under Advertisers (regional programmes exist — join the one covering the UK) and apply: https://www.awin.com/us/advertisers/partner/booking.com
- [ ] After acceptance, copy two numbers from the Awin dashboard: your **publisher ID** → `awinAffiliateId`, and Booking.com's **advertiser ID ("MID")** shown on its programme profile → `bookingAwinMid`.
- [ ] Verify: commit a hotel (type "Malmaison") → the button's URL should now start `https://www.awin1.com/cread.php?awinmid=…` and end with the Booking.com search inside `ued=`.

### 2. Trainline — via Partnerize → `trainlineCamref`
Trainline's programme runs on the Partnerize platform (commission on ticket sales, 30-day cookie).
- [ ] Apply at https://www.thetrainline.com/about-us/partnerships/affiliates — applications are reviewed, then you get a welcome pack and Partnerize dashboard access.
- [ ] In Partnerize, copy your **campaign reference** — the `camref:XXXX` token in your tracking link → paste just the `XXXX` part into `trainlineCamref`.
- [ ] Verify: commit "Edinburgh Waverley" → the button's URL should become `https://prf.hn/click/camref:XXXX/destination:…/stations/edinburgh`.

### 3. GetYourGuide (days to approve, ~8% of the activity price) → `gygPartnerId`
- [ ] Sign up at https://partner.getyourguide.com — basic details about the site and audience; approval typically takes a few days.
- [ ] Copy the **partner ID** from the partner dashboard → `gygPartnerId`. (Payout threshold €50; commission pays out after the activity happens.)
- [ ] Verify: commit "Camera Obscura" → the button's URL should carry `&partner_id=…`.

### 4. OpenTable (slowest — treat as optional) → `opentableRef`
Approval is case-by-case via the "Become a Partner" application on OpenTable's partner/developer portal, takes ~2–3 weeks, and **new affiliates start non-revenue**: revenue share opens up only after consistently referring ~100+ seated diners a month. Worth doing eventually — restaurant/café/pub is the most-typed place kind — but don't block on it.
- [ ] Apply via OpenTable's partner portal ("Become a Partner").
- [ ] Paste the assigned `ref` value → `opentableRef`.
- [ ] Verify: commit a restaurant → the button's URL should carry `&ref=…`.

{"number":133,"title":"Product requirements: two tracks (live surface, planner surface), not one","body":"Raised by the product-wiki growth pass in #132, which researched the `/plan` surface and its crowd alongside the live one. `product-wiki/product-requirements/` is human-reviewed only, so the pass recorded the implication here instead of writing it.

**The finding:** the research does not yield a single requirement set. The two surfaces serve two decisions with conflicting demands — documented with citations in the new `product-wiki/audience-divergence/` wiki. The sharpest conflicts:

- **Objective.** The planner's allocator maximises shows placed; the audience evidence favours slack (two–three shows a day, "rule of thirds", over-schedulers less satisfied). A day packed optimally also destroys the gaps the live surface exists to fill.
- **Truth.** One catalogue, two honesty obligations: sold-out is a *fact* for the live surface and a *decaying forecast* for a plan made in June.
- **Input.** Live wants zero taps; the planner's front door is a CSV produced on another site (apparently via a third-party Chrome extension).
- **Binding constraint.** Live: travel time to the next commitment. Planner: possibly accommodation, not shows — "pick my best dates" scores only show catchability.
- **Competitive claim.** Travel-aware, clash-free scheduling is table stakes on the planning side (Plan My Fringe, plus several 2026 entrants). The unoccupied ground is favourites-intake and "when should I come?" — a different claim from the live surface's reachability one.

**Suggested shape** (owner's call): `product/requirements.md` (the `executable-requirements` spec) carries two requirement tracks with their own success criteria, plus a small shared spine — catalogue, venue geometry, travel model, and the data-honesty rules — and one explicitly-owned handover requirement if the plan → live connection is wanted.

{"number":17,"title":"Claudinite handoff: 2026-07-01 — fixed-seed sort stabilizes pagination against a paginated API","body":"## Claudinite handoff bundle — 2026-07-01

Generalizable items from `[REDACTED:env:CCR_TRIGGER_REPO]` local docs not yet in the shared Claudinite canon. Each is a complete, self-contained proposal.

---

### Item 1: Pin a fixed sort seed when paging a server-sorted API to avoid duplicate/skipped rows across pages

**Source:** `scraper/fetch_shows.py`, lines 52-54:
```python
# Fixed seed so the server's ordering is stable across paged requests; without
# it a randomised sort could duplicate/skip shows between pages.
DEFAULT_SEED = "123"
```
The scraped API (`EventsSearch`) accepts a `sortBySeed` variable alongside `sortBy: "TITLE"`; the script always sends the same fixed seed string on every page request.

**Proposed addition to:** `tasks/engineeringPractices.md`, as a new bullet (no existing bullet covers pagination/sort-stability).

**Proposed wording:**
> When paging through a server-sorted API across multiple requests, pin any sort-randomization/seed parameter it exposes (e.g. a `sortBySeed`-style field) to a fixed constant. Some APIs re-randomize tie-breaking order per request when no seed is pinned — even with a stable primary sort key (e.g. `TITLE`) — so two consecutive page requests can silently reorder rows that tie on that key, causing a naive page-by-page walk to duplicate some rows and skip others with no error. A fixed seed keeps the server's ordering stable across the whole paged walk.

**Why portable:** Any project that pages through a third-party API using an offset/page-number scheme (not a cursor) can hit this — it's a common REST/GraphQL listing-API footgun, not specific to Fringe show data. The fix (pin the seed once, reuse across every page) is a one-line, broadly applicable mitigation once you know the failure mode exists.

---

Note: issue #11 (filed 2026-06-29, still open) already carries a separate pending proposal — the GitHub-hosted-runner egress workaround — which the canon has not yet absorbed (verified against the currently pinned `tasks/engineeringPractices.md`, whose datacenter-IP-blocking bullet is unchanged). {"number":6,"title":"[Prod] Real travel times (routing), not straight-line distance — incl. map-provider pricing review","body":"## Production gap: real travel times

The whole "can I reach this show in time?" logic currently estimates travel from **straight-line (haversine) distance ÷ a fixed per-mode speed** (`travelMinutes()` in `js/app.js`, with `TRAVEL_SPEEDS_KMH` for Walking / Taxi-Car / Bus / Bicycle). That's fine for a prototype but wrong in a real city: it ignores streets, the bridges/closes/hills of central Edinburgh, one-way systems, transit schedules, and traffic.

### What's needed
- Replace the distance estimate with a **real routing/ISO-distance service** that returns mode-specific durations (walking, driving, cycling, public transport).
- Ideally support **isochrones** ("everything reachable within N minutes") to draw the reach area accurately instead of a plain circle.
- Account for **departure time** (the simulated/real "now") for transit and traffic-aware driving.
- Caching strategy to keep request volume (and cost) sane — many user/destination pairs.

### Map / routing provider pricing review (part of this issue)
Compare options on capability **and cost** before committing:
- Mapbox (Directions, Matrix, Isochrone APIs)
- Google Maps Platform (Directions, Distance Matrix, Routes)
- HERE
- OpenRouteService / Valhalla / OSRM (self-hosted open-source — no per-request fee but ops cost)
- TravelTime API (isochrones first-class)
- Public-transport specifics (Traveline/Transport for Edinburgh/GTFS) for bus times

Deliverable: a short recommendation with expected request volumes and a monthly cost estimate at a few traffic tiers, plus a fallback (e.g. self-hosted OSRM) if commercial pricing is prohibitive.

### Current code touch-points
- `travelMinutes()`, `reachRadiusMeters()`, `renderReachCircle()`, `classifyShow()` in `js/app.js`.

One conversion this run.

## The prose

`edfringe-data/skills/probe-edfringe-api/SKILL.md`, step 5:

> **Delete the probe script and its workflow before opening the PR.** They are scaffolding, and a push-triggered workflow left in the tree is a live wire.

**Gate 1 — a working rule, not a product statement.** Nothing about shows, tickets, venues or what the site renders. If the product changed its mind tomorrow the rule is unchanged: it is scaffolding hygiene for the one procedure that reaches the live API. It is a rule.

**Check-the-world.** Yes — a workflow's own trigger block is a static signature. A push trigger not pinned to the default branch is exactly the shape a leftover probe has.

**Dedupe.** No existing check covers it. `gha/no-scheduled-fleet-executor` is about crons only; the other `gha/*` checks are about checkout, labels, pipefail, secrets, Pages artifacts and branch naming.

## The check

`edfringe-no-branch-push-workflow`, **blocking**, on the **edfringe-data** pack — homed there because the probe procedure is the one thing in this repo that legitimately creates such a workflow, and re-hitting the rate-limited edfringe API from a datacentre IP on every branch push is what makes the residue expensive rather than merely untidy.

**Scoped parse, not a grep.** `branches:` is a `pull_request:` filter as often as a `push:` one, and `git push` appears in `run:` steps — this repo's real workflows carry both. So the rule descends `on:` → `push:` → `branches:` by indentation, matching keys only at each block's own level, and reads nothing else in the file. It also:

- reads both sequence styles (`- main` lines and `[main, dev]`) and the inline trigger forms (`on: push`, `on: [push, pull_request]`);
- flags `branches-ignore` — it fires on every *other* branch;
- treats a **tags-only** push trigger as the release workflow it is, not a live wire;
- stays **silent** on a flow-mapping `on: {push: {...}}` rather than guessing at a shape the walk cannot read.

The failure message carries both remedies: delete the scaffolding (script included) per the probe procedure, or pin the trigger to `branches: [main]` plus `pull_request:` the way `ci.yml` does.

## Prose deleted: none

The deletion test says step 5 **stays whole**. It carries a second rule in the same breath — delete the probe *script* too — which this check does not cover, so removing only the clause the check subsumes would be a trim, and the test deletes whole or not at all.

## See-it-fail

12 fixtures, both directions proven by mutation:

- **Neuter `run()`** → all five violating-input fixtures go red (branch-scoped `branches:`, no filter at all, both inline trigger forms, `branches-ignore`); clean fixtures stay green.
- **Replace the scoped walk with a naive two-token grep** → the clean fixtures go red instead, including the live gate over this repo's five real workflow files.

`bash scripts/verify.sh` green (190/190 tests, JS + Python syntax, normalizer self-test). `check_the_world.mjs`: **0 blocking** — the single advisory is a pre-existing `file-placement` one on `plan/lib/search.js`, untouched here.

## Scope

Exactly the check module, its `pack.mjs` registration, and its fixtures. Nothing under `.claudinite/shared/` touched; no pack outside `edfringe-data`.

name: CI

# The static-site repo's PR gate, vendored from the static-website pack. Three
# things every pull request must pass, and deliberately NO `paths:` filter on
# the trigger: a path-filtered conformance flow arms auto-merge and then never
# runs, so the repo's own maintenance PR waits forever (the basics
# `conformance-workflow` rule).
#
#   conformance  the Claudinite world sweep from this repo's own mount.
#   gate         the repo's `test_command` ("" = it stated it has none).
#   assemble     a dry run of the release's artifact assembly — the publish set
#                is built exactly as the deploy builds it, so a renamed file or
#                a stale `publish_paths` entry fails on the PR instead of
#                silently dropping a page from the live site.
#
# workflow_dispatch so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose open GitHub never turns
# into a pull_request run) can still have this suite started on its branch.
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  ci:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # The PR's real head, not the synthetic merge commit, so CI evaluates
          # what the session's own Stop hook does.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}

# EdFringeNow — executable UI/UX requirements

What the site's two front-ends must render and how they must behave — Part I
the **Now** page, Part II the **Plan** page. Each numbered leaf is proven by
exactly one executable case; the image under a leaf **is** its expected
rendering, cropped to just what that leaf asserts.

<details><summary>How this document works</summary>

The feature-level story of what the product is and why lives in
[docs/product-spec.md](../docs/product-spec.md); this document holds only
statements a test can prove.

Every leaf is executed by exactly one case under
[product/requirements/](requirements/) — see its
[README](requirements/README.md) for the framework: kinds, runners, goldens,
the coverage gate, and how to add or change a requirement. The committed
golden images and coded assertions are the **owner's approval record**: an
agent may propose a new expected, but never changes a committed one to make a
red case pass — on a mismatch it surfaces actual vs expected and asks.

**Numbering.** Every leaf carries a stable id (e.g. `6.4`). Add new
requirements under new numbers; never renumber or reuse a retired one. Each
leaf has exactly one case named `<slug>.<id>.case.js`; the case's *kind* is the
folder it lives in (`screen/` — a pixel-exact golden cropped to the leaf's
scope; `behavior/` — a driven gesture asserted in code; `logic/` — a pure rule
proved against the shipped module). The line under each leaf tagged
`req-gallery` is machine-managed (the gallery generator rewrites it); the prose
is hand-authored.

**The reference moment.** Visual cases render at **Sat 15 Aug 2026, 19:30**
Edinburgh time, from a fixed fake location in central Edinburgh, against the
frozen fixture dataset ([requirements/shared/reference-now.js](requirements/shared/reference-now.js)).
</details>

> ⚠️ **A green build means "claimed", not "fully verified".** The visual cases
> render the real pages in a real (headless, pinned) Chromium, but the network
> is faked from committed fixtures, external links are asserted as URLs and
> never followed, real geolocation/GPS/device clocks are substituted with fixed
> fakes, and downloads are read back as bytes rather than imported anywhere.
> The fixture dataset is a frozen, curated snapshot of the real committed data
> — provenance and its two documented adjustments in
> [requirements/shared/fixtures/build-fixtures.js](requirements/shared/fixtures/build-fixtures.js).

---

# Part I — the Now page

## 1. Page chrome

- `1.1` The desktop header: logo, centred **Now | Plan** nav with **Now** active, location button.

  ![now-chrome.1.1](requirements/screen/cases/now-chrome.1.1.png) <!-- req-gallery:1.1 -->

  <details><summary>Notes</summary>

  The logo reads `EdFringe` + red `Now`; the nav links are `Now` (`./`, active) and `Plan` (`plan/`); the location button carries `aria-label="Use my location"`. Header is sticky, white, 64px.
  </details>

- `1.2` Below 860px the nav is gone — logo and location button only.
